title: v1/chat.completions: parameter translation layer and tool-capability negotiator
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation and summary: This PR implements a dedicated parameter translation layer in the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility adapter and adds a lightweight tool-capability negotiation handshake for function/tool calling. Our goal is to reduce edge-case mismatches between client v1 params and Redwood's internal runtime while improving streaming resilience when tool calls are present. Context: customers have hit subtle regressions when mixing stop arrays, logprobs requests, and function/tool calls across streaming and non-streaming paths. Previously we tried to fold fixes into the stream coordinator; this approach centralizes translation rules and capability negotiation to make behavior deterministic and easier to test. What this PR does (high level): - Add a v1->internal param translation module that: maps role conventions (role aliases/namespaces), normalizes stop semantics (string vs array vs null), and synthesizes logprob requests into internal token-level profiling hooks without enabling expensive backprop-like work paths. - Introduce a tool-capability negotiator: during stream handshake we emit a concise capability token that advertises whether the server can perform structured tool calls in-stream (framed tool output) vs deferred tool-resolution. Clients that lack parity fall back to non-streamed tool call semantics. - Streaming stability changes: fragment coalescing window expanded for fragments that contain a tool invocation token; added a 100ms minimum inter-fragment delay on tool fragments to avoid parser races in clients that buffer up to N fragments. - Structured output: introduce an optional v1 flag `structured_response=true` (back-ported via translation) that generates a framed JSON envelope for tool outputs and assistant final messages, preserving both role metadata and function-call metadata in a single `envelope` object. - Stop/logprob harmonization: implement a normalization pass that: removes duplicate stop tokens, ensures stop precedence with function-call terminators, and emits a per-response `logprob_summary` when clients request `logprobs` while streaming (we avoid full token-by-token logprob streaming to control overhead). - Backwards compat notes: translation layer is conservative—if an unknown or conflicting param is provided we log a compat warning and fall back to historical behavior. Tests and coverage: included unit tests for role aliasing, stop array coalescing, capability negotiation handshake, and an integration test that runs the streaming handshake + function call against a mock tool. Checklist: - [x] Parameter translation module implemented with feature flag (off by default in non-v1 flows) - [x] Tool-capability negotiator added to stream handshake - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs inline comments and a short note to the compatibility guide - [x] Benchmarked: small regression (<1% latency p95) on standard load - [x] E2E validation against OpenAI-compat test vectors Caveats and follow-ups: - The structured_response flag is experimental; we will gate it by a flag until we verify interop with beta SDKs. - We observed a flaky test in the first CI run related to websocket teardown; fixed by adding a bounded close timeout and a retry in the mock harness. Related Linear items and followups: ENG-2419 (v1 compat parameter gaps), ENG-2475 (streaming functioncall parser hardening), ENG-2631 (structured output evaluation). Links: Linear/ENG-2419, RFC:docs/rfcs/v1-param-translation.md
